title: A Noetherian local ring of finite global dimension is regular (Serre)
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which has finite global dimension [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Then $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00OC (proposition-finite-gl-dim-regular, line 27096), implication (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3) through (1) ($\kappa$ has finite projective dimension), with its proof (Lemmas length-resolution-residue-field and dim-gl-dim); also the first sentence of Lemma Tag 0AFS

proof.text: $\kappa$ has finite projective dimension ((2) $\Rightarrow$ (1) of 00OC, 'trivial'). Since $R$ has finite global dimension [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], there is an integer $N\ge0$ such that every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le N$; in particular the $R$-module $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ has one, i.e. $\kappa$ has finite projective dimension.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00OC (proposition-finite-gl-dim-regular, line 27096), proof lines 27109-27115

proof.text: $D=\dim R$ is finite and $\kappa$ has a projective resolution of length $\le D$. The Krull dimension $D$ of the Noetherian local ring $R$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters]. By Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-pd-le-krull-dimension] (Stacks Lemma 00OB), $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\le D$, i.e. $\kappa$ has a projective resolution $0\to P_D\to\dots\to P_0\to\kappa\to0$ of length $\le D$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00OC (proposition-finite-gl-dim-regular, line 27096), proof lines 27109-27115

proof.text: $\dim R\ge\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Let $n=\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-pd-ge-embedding-dimension] (Stacks Lemma 00OA) to the projective resolution of $\kappa$ of length $\le D$ from Step 2 (with $d=D$) gives $D\ge n$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00OC (proposition-finite-gl-dim-regular, line 27096), proof lines 27109-27115

proof.text: $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $n$ elements. $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so the ideal $\mathfrak m$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, and $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m\cdot\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is a $\kappa$-vector space of dimension $n$. Choose $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathfrak m$ whose images form a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ (as in the proof of Stacks 00OA). Their images generate $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m\mathfrak m$, so by Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] applied to the finitely generated module $M=\mathfrak m$, the elements $x_1,\dots,x_n$ generate $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00OC, proof line 27115 ('Thus $R$ is regular, see Definition regular-local and the discussion preceding it'); the discussion before Definition 00KU (definition-regular-local, line 14615): minimal number of generators of m equals dim m/m^2 by Nakayama, Lemma 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: $R$ is regular. By Steps 3 and 4, $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $x_1,\dots,x_n$ together with $D-n\ge0$ copies of $0$, that is by $D=\dim R$ elements. As $R$ is a Noetherian local ring, this is the definition of a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 00OC (2) => (1) => (3) and kept it. Mathlib (searched with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle and grep) has IsRegularLocalRing and projective dimension (pd(M/xM)=pd M+1, pd of quotients by regular sequences, localization) but neither direction of Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre, nor any bound relating pd of the residue field to m/m^2 or to dim R. Wrote the proof of 00OC in five steps: finite gl.dim gives a finite projective resolution of kappa (instance of the definition); dim R finite (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters) and pd kappa <= dim R (new node, Stacks 00OB); dim m/m^2 <= dim R (new node, Stacks 00OA, applied to that resolution, so the minimum of lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-well-defined is not needed); m generated by dim m/m^2 elements by Nakayama (existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators); padding with zeros gives dim R generators, the definition in def-weil-regular-scheme. The Stacks route is 00OA + 00OB (Koszul complex and Buchsbaum-Eisenbud depth bound), not an 'infinite minimal resolution over a non-regular ring' argument; the split follows Stacks. stmt_deps unchanged. Two new unsplit nodes.

reviewed.note: 5 steps following Stacks 00OC (2)=>(1)=>(3): kappa has finite projective dimension; dim R finite (system of parameters leaf) and pd kappa <= dim R (new unsplit 00OB node); pd kappa >= dim m/m^2 (new unsplit 00OA node, applied to a resolution of length <= dim R); Nakayama lifts a basis of m/m^2 to generators of m; padding by zeros gives dim R generators. Not in Mathlib (no Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre). Tags 00OA, 00OB, 00OC verified.
